Counts refer to people: 62 Chinese university students participated and the final sample was 62. Both conditions use the same participants; the two condition counts of 62 must not be added. No participant exclusion or attrition count is reported.

The comparison is between two generative-AI configurations: standard ChatGPT-4 and personalised Mr. Ranedeer, both described as based on GPT-4 architecture. Students could freely enter prompts and adjust the interaction flow; the personalised condition used learner settings and an adaptive learning plan (PDF p. 5, printed p. 169, GenAI feedback conditions; PDF p. 8, printed p. 172, Measures; Appendix Tables A1?A2, PDF pp. 20?21, printed pp. 184?185).

The product-improvement task asked for three original and useful improvement solutions for a stuffed bunny and a portable coffee maker using the assigned GenAI tool. Mean completion times were standard 17 minutes (SD = 7) and personalised 20 minutes (SD = 6), with a 5-minute break (PDF pp. 7?8, printed pp. 171?172, CPS performance and Procedure; Figure 3 on PDF p. 9, printed p. 173).

Quality, elaboration and originality were scored on the produced solutions by two trained raters blinded to condition, using a 5-point scale; final scores were averaged across raters. The construct codes usefulness, elaboration and novelty and the with_ai question match these measures; the comparison is within-person (PDF pp. 7?8, printed pp. 171?172, CPS performance; PDF p. 11, printed p. 175, Table 2).

The one-line finding accurately combines the final sample of 62 with higher personalised-condition quality (3.50 vs 3.08; p = .001) and elaboration (3.58 vs 2.48; p < .001), and no statistically significant originality difference (2.92 vs 3.13; p = 0.098) (PDF p. 5, printed p. 169, Participants; PDF p. 11, printed p. 175, Table 2 and accompanying Results).
